prompt.text:
Implement deterministic segment correspondence in `solution.rs` using only the standard library.

Expose:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Segment {
    pub first: usize,
    pub second: usize,
    pub squared_length: u64,
    pub low_angle: i32,
    pub high_angle: i32,
    pub orientation: i32,
    pub reversed: bool,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Correspondence {
    pub probe_index: usize,
    pub gallery_index: usize,
    pub orientation_delta: i32,
    pub score: u64,
}

pub fn match_segments(
    probe: &[Segment],
    gallery: &[Segment],
    length_tolerance: u64,
    angle_tolerance: i32,
    strict: bool,
) -> Vec<Correspondence>;
```

Angles use degrees and must be compared by their shortest circular distance modulo 360. A negative `angle_tolerance` permits no matches. Lengths match when their absolute difference is at most `length_tolerance`. Both low and high angles must match. In strict mode, omit only the final probe segment; an empty probe remains empty.

For a match, compute `orientation_delta` as gallery orientation minus probe orientation. Negate the gallery orientation first when `reversed` differs between the two segments. Normalize the delta to `[-180, 179]`. The score is `abs(length difference) + circular(low-angle difference) + circular(high-angle difference)`. Preserve probe-major then gallery-major ordering, retain all qualifying matches, and do not mutate either input.

Return only the complete source file; do not include Markdown fences or prose.
